transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess I’m here because I’ve been worrying a lot, and I can’t really shut it off. Once something gets in my head—my mother getting up at night, a grant report, whether I missed something at work—I just keep turning it over, even if I make lists or try to think about something else.
Do you ever feel the need to perform specific rituals or repetitive behaviors to reduce your anxiety or worries?
No, not really. I mean, I might check a note or a list again, but I don’t think I have rituals or anything like that.
Do you have unwanted thoughts that keep coming back to you?

Yes… I mean, not like bizarre thoughts, exactly. More like once I start worrying about something—my mother getting up at night, a grant report, whether I missed something at work—it just keeps coming back. I try making lists or redirecting myself, but it doesn’t really… go away.
Do you ever feel like you must repeat certain behaviors to prevent something bad from happening?
I don’t think so. I might double-check things sometimes, but it doesn’t feel like I have to repeat something to stop something bad from happening.
Do you feel an overwhelming urge to repeat certain actions or mental acts?
Not overwhelming, no. I don’t think I get urges like that. I might go back over something in my head, but it’s not… like I have to repeat an action or anything.
Do you often feel restless or on edge?
I’m not sure… maybe sometimes. I wouldn’t say I notice it all the time, but I do feel kind of keyed up now and then.
Do you worry about everyday things, like finances, health, or relationships, more than most people?

Yes… I think so. It used to mostly be about my mother’s safety, but this past year it’s sort of spread—money, decisions at work, deadlines, the house… whether I’m doing enough as a daughter. Even small things can start to feel like they’re going to unravel.
Has your worrying been interfering with your daily activities or relationships?

Yes… a bit. At work especially. I’ve been missing small but important details at the library, which isn’t really like me. And I had to hand off parts of a grant presentation after I just… froze. I don’t like saying that, but it’s made me wonder if I’m still doing a good job leading my team.
Do you ever experience sudden, intense episodes of fear or anxiety that reach a peak within minutes?
I don’t think so. I mean… I get anxious, but I wouldn’t say it comes on suddenly like that or peaks within minutes.
Do you often feel tense in your muscles?

Yes… mostly by the end of the day. My neck and shoulders get really tight, like I’ve been bracing without noticing. And I catch myself clenching my jaw sometimes, especially with emails or when I’m listening for my mother in the other room.
Do you have periods where your anxiety suddenly becomes much worse?
I’m not sure I’d call it “suddenly.” It sort of… builds, I guess. I have worse moments, but not like a switch flipping.
Is there one main thing that you worry about most of the time?

It used to mostly be my mother’s safety. But… this past year it’s kind of spread. Finances, work decisions, deadlines, the house… whether I’m doing enough as a daughter. Even small things can start feeling like they’re going to unravel.
Is there a specific situation or thing that usually triggers your worrying?

Not one specific thing, no. It used to be mostly my mother and whether she was safe, but now it can be… money, work deadlines, decisions with staff, things around the house. Even small things sometimes start feeling like they’re going to turn into something bigger.
Have you ever had a panic attack?
I don’t think so. I mean, I’ve had times where I felt really anxious, but I’m not sure I’d call it a panic attack.
Can you describe what happens during those times when you feel really anxious?

It’s usually not dramatic, exactly. A worry starts—like my mother getting up at night, or a grant report, or whether I missed something at work—and then I just… can’t put it away. I make lists, I try to think about something else, but it stays there and keeps circling.
Have you ever had a period of intense fear or discomfort that reached a peak within minutes and included symptoms like a racing heart, sweating, or shortness of breath?
No… I don’t think I’ve had something like that, where it suddenly peaks in a few minutes. I get very anxious, but it feels more drawn out than that.
Is your worrying usually about one or two main things, or is it spread across many different areas of your life?

It’s… more than one or two things now. It used to be mostly about my mother’s safety, but over the past year it’s kind of spread—money, work deadlines, staff decisions, the house. Even small things can start to feel like they might unravel if I don’t stay on top of them.
Is there a particular area of your life where your worries seem to be most prominent?

I guess it isn’t just one area anymore. It started mostly with worrying about my mother being safe, but now it’s… finances, work deadlines, staff decisions, the house. And then I start wondering if I’m doing enough as a daughter. Even small things can feel like they’re about to unravel if I don’t keep track of them.
Is your worrying spread across most areas of your life, including work, finances, relationships, and daily responsibilities?

Yes… I think so. It started with worrying about my mother’s safety, but over the past year it’s spread to money, work deadlines, staff decisions, the house… and whether I’m doing enough as a daughter. Even small things can feel like they might unravel if I’m not careful.
